title: Reflection of the zipper tape
statement: For an alphabet $A$, an integer frontier $z$, and finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, the tape represented by frontier $z$ and stacks $l,r$ equals the tape represented by frontier $-(z-1)$ and stacks $r,l$, evaluated at the reflected coordinate: for every $w\in\mathbb{Z}$, the first tape's content at $w$ is the second tape's content at $-w$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols
replaced:
Let $z$ be an integer and let $l$ and $r$ be finite lists of possibly-blank
symbols over an alphabet $A$. The two-stack zipper tape with frontier $z$,
left stack $l$, and right stack $r$ coincides, as a function on $\mathbb{Z}$,
with the coordinate reflection $w \mapsto$ (zipper tape with frontier
$-(z - 1)$, left stack $r$, and right stack $l$, read at $-w$): reversing the
scanning direction exchanges the two stacks.
